newsitem.title: USA: Bristol-Myers has pediatric dosage of Zerit.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers has pediatric dosage of Zerit.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said Thursday the availability of an oral solution formulation of the company's Zerit represents a significant addition to the therapeutic options available to treat HIV-infected infants and children.
The company has sold the drug -- stavudine, d4T -- in the U.S. since 1994 in the form of a pill for adults, spokesman John Kouten said.
He pointed out the drug is now one of four available for treatment of pediatric AIDS, while nine are available for treatment of adults.

Zeirt for Oral Solution is a fruit-flavored powder in bottles providing 200 ml of a 1 mg/ml stavudine solution upon constitution with water, the company said. Zerit is a nucleoside analogue that inhibits the action of reverse transcriptase, a vital enzyme the AIDS virus uses to reproduce itself.
